ONE_LINE: Consolidation REORGANIZES memory; it does not decide truth.

SCOPE_DISCIPLINE.authoritative: The append-only event log written by VERIFIED_MEMORY_WRITE_V1 remains the ONLY authoritative state. Consolidation reads it and produces DERIVED state.
SCOPE_DISCIPLINE.explicitly_forbidden: Consolidation may NOT resolve a contradiction, pick a winner among conflicting values, infer supersession from timestamps, delete or rewrite a canonical record, or change any verification state. Those are truth decisions; this milestone is reorganization. A consolidation that 'cleans up' a disagreement has destroyed information the memory is supposed to carry.
SCOPE_DISCIPLINE.pipeline: event log -> deterministic replay -> derived consolidated state -> retrieval index

HEADLINE_INVARIANT.why_it_matters: If a store can ingest N events incrementally, have all derived state discarded, replay the immutable log from scratch, and produce an IDENTICAL consolidated-state hash, then derived state is provably a pure function of the log. That is the foundation continuous learning needs: it means no derived artifact can silently drift away from the canonical history.
HEADLINE_INVARIANT.how_it_is_tested_honestly: Two GENUINELY DIFFERENT implementations are compared, not one function called twice. (a) ConsolidationIndex is maintained INCREMENTALLY, one event at a time, with its own indexes. (b) consolidate_from_scratch() computes every group by a fresh full scan over the replayed record map, using no incremental structure. C9 asserts their state hashes are equal. The bug classes this actually catches: retraction failing to dissolve a group, mutation aliasing between snapshots, non-deterministic iteration order, stale index entries, and missed invalidation.

ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C1_deterministic_replay: Replaying the same log twice yields identical consolidated-state hashes; hashing is canonical (sorted, no set/dict iteration order dependence, no wall-clock input).
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C2_derived_state_fully_rebuildable: Deleting every derived artifact (snapshot, indexes) and rebuilding from the log alone reproduces the same state hash.
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C3_canonical_records_never_mutated: Consolidation never writes to the event log and never alters a ClaimRecord's canonical fields; asserted by hashing the log before and after.
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C4_contradictions_preserved: Conflicting claims remain BOTH active and BOTH grouped as a contradiction; consolidation never reduces a contradiction group to one member.
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C5_explicit_supersession_only: No supersession is inferred. A later observed_at with no explicit link leaves both records active and contradicting.
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C6_retractions_removed_from_active_retri: Retracted records are absent from the current-state projection and from the retrieval index, while remaining in the log and in all_records().
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C7_provenance_survives_duplicate_cluster: Clustering duplicates never collapses provenance: every member's source_id, observed_at_utc and record_id remain individually recoverable from the cluster.
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C8_certified_reader_unchanged: assert_certified_memory_v1_unchanged() holds across consolidation, and consolidation imports nothing from the certified reasoning path.
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C10_cache_invalidation_follows_state_has: The retrieval index is bound to the consolidated-state hash; any change to active membership changes that hash and therefore the reader's backend cache key. Includes a demonstration that a stale index WOULD have served removed records.
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C11_crash_restart_recovery: A process dying at any stage of the commit sequence must leave canonical state recoverable and derived state reconstructible.
ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.C12_event_order_replay_invariants: Events replay in log order; the log is append-only (a prefix of the log at version N is byte-identical to the log as it stood at version N).

commit_sequence: 1. append canonical event to the log
4. atomically publish the snapshot (write temp -> fsync -> os.replace)
C11_CRASH_SAFETY_PROTOCOL.recovery_rule: If the process dies between ANY two stages, the canonical event log alone is sufficient. A snapshot is only ever an accelerator: it is validated against the log it claims to describe (corpus_version + log hash) and DISCARDED on any mismatch, then rebuilt.
C11_CRASH_SAFETY_PROTOCOL.why_atomic_publish: os.replace is atomic on POSIX, so a snapshot is either fully present or absent -- never half-written. Without it, a crash mid-write would leave a corrupt snapshot that a naive reader would trust.
failure_modes_tested: crash after append but before snapshot (stale/missing snapshot)
crash mid-snapshot-write (partial temp file must never be published)
snapshot describing a DIFFERENT log (hash mismatch -> discard and rebuild)
truncated final log line (partial append) -- must not corrupt replay

ALIAS_HANDLING.scope: Aliases are clustered from EXPLICIT alias claims only (relation 'alias_of'). No alias is inferred from string similarity, co-occurrence, or embedding proximity -- inference is a truth decision and is out of scope.
ALIAS_HANDLING.effect: Alias clusters allow consolidation to group support/contradiction across names that explicit evidence says are the same entity. This is REORGANIZATION: it changes how records are grouped and reported, never which records are active and never a verification state.
ALIAS_HANDLING.separation_from_ingest: Ingest-time conflict detection stays LOCAL and cheap (raw claim key). Alias-aware grouping is GLOBAL and happens only in consolidation. The two are allowed to disagree, and that is by design -- a later alias claim can reveal a contradiction that was invisible at ingest time.

PRESSURE_TEST.when: Only after C1-C12 pass. Correctness first.
PRESSURE_TEST.workload: 100k-1M synthetic events mixing new claims, exact duplicates, aliases, conflicts, supersessions and retractions.
measure: incremental update latency (per-event, and its distribution)
consolidation drift (incremental vs rebuild hash at checkpoints)
PRESSURE_TEST.purpose: Begin answering how much this living memory can ingest and what hardware it actually needs. Results are reported as measurements, not as a pass/fail gate -- there is no frozen performance threshold, and inventing one after seeing the numbers would be exactly the post-hoc move this project avoids.
PRESSURE_TEST.honest_expectation: A full O(n) replay is expected to become the dominant cost as the log grows. If it does, that is a finding to report and the motivation for a later checkpoint/compaction design -- not something to hide behind a snapshot that is never validated.

GPU_REQUIRED: NONE. This milestone is entirely CPU-bound. The Lightning balance blocker is irrelevant to it, and no top-up is warranted until a GPU-dependent experiment actually exists.
NOT_A_QUALITY_CLAIM: Like MILESTONE_1, this is a CAPABILITY and CORRECTNESS milestone. No quality gate is run and none is implied.
